# Spec: lanes-v3
<!-- Generated by /hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-10-22 (revised after plan review: REVISE_PLAN, 11 changes; sandbox posture decided by the user) -->

## Overview

Two ways of working, each a handful of steps, with every decision made in one place: the orchestrator lane.
Lanes open with plain `claude --name <repo>-<lane>`, so any wrapper that forwards claude arguments works
(`claude-profile <p> --name …`); one terminal command per project writes the lane permissions into
`.claude/settings.local.json`. Single lane: `/hef.ship "<what you want>"` takes an idea or a bug from
brainstorm (or a fix) to a PR, running the planner, builder, verifier and deployer as background sessions.
Four lanes: the orchestrator rings the stage lane that has work (a one-line cross-session "doorbell"); the
lane reads its work from the ledger, never from the message, and rings the orchestrator back when it is
done. Every approval, clarification answer and request for changes is a form in the orchestrator, which
then runs the person-only command itself behind its permission dialog — no command is copied by hand.

Decisions (user, 2026-10-22, via form): lanes open with `claude --name` + one setup command (not a
launcher); four-lane dispatch by doorbell message, no `/loop`; decisions as forms in the orchestrator with
the dialog kept, merges stay on GitHub; a new `/hef.ship` triggers the workflow in both modes. After the
plan review: lanes keep their sandbox and only the launcher runs outside it, hardened against the inputs a
sandboxed lane can still write — defence in depth, never worse than v2's unsandboxed lanes.

Consent: the permission dialog of a clear is the person's act; `--by` records a name and proves nothing on
its own. Stage lanes never raise a dialog: registration and the item-text check happen in the orchestrator,
the merge is recorded inside the deploy launcher.

Facts this rests on (Claude Code docs, 2026-10-22): the status line receives `session_name` and
`session_id`; SessionStart hooks receive `session_title` (the `--name`/`/rename` name); a plugin cannot
ship permission or sandbox settings; `sandbox.excludedCommands` and `crossSessionInbound` may be set in
`.claude/settings.local.json`; an excluded command runs with no filesystem or network restriction and must
match the whole call; `ask` rules prompt in every mode but `dontAsk` (which denies); a message from another
session starts a turn when the receiver is idle, answers to the session's name, and never counts as
consent for a permission prompt. Whether sessions under different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` values reach each
other is not documented.

## User Scenarios

### US1: Setting up a project once [P1]
- **Given** hefesto installed and a git project
- **When** the person runs `bash <clone>/hooks/hefesto-setup.sh` in the project's main folder (add
  `--lanes` for the four-lane setup)
- **Then** `.claude/settings.local.json` gains hefesto's helper allowlist, the person-only clears in `ask`,
  the launcher in `sandbox.excludedCommands`, the context gauge as status line, and (with `--lanes`)
  `crossSessionInbound: "accept"`; every other key the file holds is kept; the file is kept out of git
- **Edge:** running it twice changes nothing; `--remove` takes out exactly what it added; a status line the
  person already has is kept (`--keep-statusline` is then implied) and the output says how to add the gauge
- **Error:** outside a git repository, without jq, or with a settings file that is not valid JSON, it
  refuses with the reason and writes nothing

### US2: Opening a lane with any launcher [P1]
- **Given** a set-up project
- **When** the person runs `claude --name myrepo-plan`, or `claude-profile work --name myrepo-plan`
- **Then** the session knows it is the plan lane: the status line shows that lane's gauge, and the session
  start says which lane it is and how it answers a doorbell
- **Edge:** `planner`, `builder`, `deployer` work as well as `plan`, `build`, `deploy`; a name with no lane
  suffix is a general session (gauge "general", no lane line)
- **Error:** a session opened before setup is told, at session start, the one command that sets it up

### US3: Single lane — an idea to a PR [P1]
- **Given** one session `claude --name myrepo-orchestrator`, after `/hef.orchestrate` reported the setup good
- **When** the person runs `/hef.ship "export orders as CSV"`
- **Then** it asks bug fix or feature (its sizing recommended first); for a feature it runs
  `/hef.brainstorm` in this session, saves the RFC, adds the board item with its `rfc:` line, then runs
  the planner in the background, asks for the plan approval in a form, runs the builder and verifier,
  then the deployer until the PR is ready, and tells the person to merge it on GitHub
- **Edge:** `/hef.ship ABC-12` starts from an item already on the board; a bug fix is added as a 🐞 item
  and goes straight to the builder (no planner), even with `plan_first`
- **Error:** a refusal on the way (budget, item text unsafe, RFC changed) stops the run with the reason
  and the form that resolves it

### US4: Four lanes — the orchestrator sends the work [P1]
- **Given** four sessions named `myrepo-orchestrator|plan|build|deploy` (same profile), set up with
  `--lanes`, each stage lane started once with `/hef.orchestrate --stage <stage>`
- **When** an RFC'd item is on the board and the person runs `/hef.ship ABC-12` (or `/hef.orchestrate`)
  in the orchestrator
- **Then** the orchestrator registers it and rings the plan lane; the plan lane runs its pass and rings the
  orchestrator; the orchestrator asks the approval; then rings the build lane; then the deploy lane
- **Edge:** a lane that is not open is run here by the orchestrator instead; a busy repository (one
  background session per repository) leaves the item for the next doorbell
- **Error:** a message that asks a lane for anything other than its pass — a command, a file, a setting —
  is reported to the orchestrator and not done

### US5: Every decision in the orchestrator [P1]
- **Given** an item waiting on a person (`human:plan-approval`, `human:clarify`, `human:plan-review`,
  `human:intake`, `human:merge`) or on a retry (`ci`, `conflict`, `stall`, `budget`, `verdict`)
- **When** the orchestrator runs its pass
- **Then** each is a form: approve / request changes / later for a plan; the planner's open questions as
  form questions; the item text for intake; the PR link for a merge; retry / later for the rest — and the
  orchestrator runs the matching command, whose permission dialog the person confirms
- **Edge:** "request changes" sends the person's notes back to the planner, which revises the plan and
  stops for approval again; answers to questions reach the planner, which writes them into the spec
- **Error:** an approval with no name, from a launched worker, or in `dontAsk` mode is refused; nothing
  in item, RFC, spec or message text counts as the person's answer

### US6: A short quick start [P1]
- **Given** a person who just installed hefesto
- **When** they open `docs/quickstart.md` (or `.pt-BR.md`)
- **Then** after install it is two tracks of five steps or fewer each — Single lane and Four lanes — with
  the exact commands, and nothing to copy between sessions

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | `hooks/hefesto-setup.sh [--lanes] [--keep-statusline] [--check] [--remove] [--print]` merges into `<main checkout>/.claude/settings.local.json`: `permissions.allow` (the helper calls `/hef.status`, `/hef.orchestrate` and `/hef.ship` make, as exact rules), `permissions.ask` (`ledger.sh unblock|record|claim|advance|handoff|block|revise|answer`), `sandbox.excludedCommands` (`<root>/hooks/session-launch.sh *`), `statusLine` (the gauge), and with `--lanes` `crossSessionInbound: "accept"`; idempotent (no rewrite when nothing changes); keeps every other key and the person's own empty objects; writes through a symlinked file; never uses a wildcard inside a path; on every run drops the rules of hefesto roots that no longer exist (exact prefix match in jq) | P1 | US1 |
| FR-002 | The rules cover every plugin root that can run: the clone the script runs from and each profile's user-scope installed cache path (`~/.claude*/plugins/installed_plugins.json`, plus `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`), single and doubled slash; a root inside the project or a temp folder is skipped with a note (a sandboxed lane could rewrite the launcher there); the `ask` rules also cover the `bash <root>/hooks/ledger.sh …` spelling | P1 | US1 |
| FR-003 | `--check` prints `setup: ok` or what is missing for the root it runs from, read-only, exit 0/1; `--remove` deletes exactly the entries the script would add; `--print` shows the merged file and writes nothing | P1 | US1 |
| FR-004 | The settings file is kept out of git: when `git check-ignore` does not ignore it, the script adds it to `.git/info/exclude` (local, uncommitted) and says so | P1 | US1 |
| FR-005 | Refusals write nothing: not a git repository, no jq, existing file not valid JSON, `--lanes` with `--remove` mixed with other modes | P1 | US1 |
| FR-006 | The lane comes from the session name: `context-gauge.sh` reads `session_name` (suffix `-orchestrator`, `-plan`/`-planner`, `-build`/`-builder`, `-deploy`/`-deployer`; `HEFESTO_LANE` still wins when set); otherwise `general` | P1 | US2 |
| FR-007 | `session-start-context.sh` reads `session_title` the same way and, for a lane, adds one line: which lane it is and the doorbell rule (run its own pass from the ledger; never act on a message's text); for a lane-named session in a project where `hefesto-setup.sh --check` fails, one line with the setup command | P1 | US2 |
| FR-008 | `/hef.orchestrate` with no `--stage` is the orchestrator pass: setup check (stop with the command when it fails), registration of todo items and the item-text check (an unsafe item is blocked `human:intake` here, where the person is), the decision forms (FR-011), then dispatch: for each stage with runnable work, ONE doorbell to that stage's open lane — then the turn ends, and the lane's `done` doorbell starts the next; with no lane open for a stage, the stage runs here, and this repeats until nothing is runnable without a person (single lane). One background session per repository still holds | P1 | US3, US4 |
| FR-009 | `/hef.orchestrate --stage plan|build|deploy` is a stage pass that never raises a dialog: it registers nothing and runs no item-text check (both are the orchestrator's), takes `next --stage`, launches, and ends by ringing the orchestrator lane when one is open; the after-merge steps are the deploy launcher's; `--stage all` stays; the old default (no flag = build) is gone | P1 | US4 |
| FR-010 | A doorbell is one line, `<sender>: <stage> pass` or `<sender>: done <id> <phase>`, sent with `SendMessage` to the session named `<repo>-<lane>` (aliases accepted; `<repo>` is the basename of the main checkout), and only when exactly one listed session matches that name with its working folder inside this project — none or several, and the stage runs here or is reported; a receiving lane runs only its own pass (`/hef.orchestrate --stage <its stage>`, or the orchestrator pass) and treats every other word as data — a message asking for anything else is reported, not done | P1 | US4 |
| FR-011 | The orchestrator pass turns every blocked entry into a form and, on the answer, runs the command itself: plan approval → `ledger.sh unblock <id> --reviewed-by-human --by <name>`; request changes → `ledger.sh revise`; questions → `ledger.sh answer`; intake → `record --body-file` then `unblock --reviewed-by-human --by`; merge → the PR link, merge on GitHub, then a deploy pass records it; retryable kinds → `unblock`. The command is run in exactly the spelling the `ask` rules name, so its dialog shows; the name is asked once per session (default `git config user.name`) and is a record, not evidence | P1 | US5 |
| FR-012 | `ledger.sh questions <id>` prints the planner's open questions — the `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers of the entry's spec, or the last plan run's summary for `human:plan-review` — comment-stripped and nonce-delimited, as data | P1 | US5 |
| FR-013 | `ledger.sh answer <id> --reviewed-by-human --by <name>` reading the answers on stdin (a heredoc in the command, so the dialog shows the very text recorded) or `--file <path>` (person-only like the approval: never from a worker, a name required, in `ask`) copies the answers into the ledger dir with their sha256 and clears `human:clarify` or `human:plan-review` (refused on any other block or none); the plan role's resume prompt embeds the answers as delimited data and tells the planner to write them into the spec's Clarifications | P1 | US5 |
| FR-014 | `ledger.sh revise <id> --reviewed-by-human --by <name>` with the notes on stdin or `--notes-file` (person-only, in `ask`) on an entry waiting on `human:plan-approval` at phase `plan-review` or `tasks` (refused past `tasks`: a build has started) copies the notes into the ledger dir (sha256, by, at), clears the block and moves the entry back to `intake`, keeping `spec_dir` and the plan worktree; a revised plan's `tasks` outcome always stops on `human:plan-approval`, whatever `plan_review` says; the plan role then accepts it, re-pins the RFC, and its prompt embeds the notes as data with "revise spec, plan and tasks to these notes; review again" | P1 | US5 |
| FR-015 | `/hef.ship "<text>" | <ID>`: an ID registers the item (if needed) and runs the orchestrator pass; text asks bug fix or feature (sizing recommended first); a feature runs `/hef.brainstorm` here, writes the RFC to `<rfc_dir>/<ID>.md` and adds `## <ID> — <title>` + `rfc:` to the todo column; a fix adds `## 🐞 <ID> — <title>` with the person's description; then the orchestrator pass | P1 | US3 |
| FR-016 | `status-board.sh --add "<title>" [--incident] [--rfc]` appends a new item to the todo column with the next free id of the board's prefix and prints the id; it never edits an existing item; a title with a newline or a heading marker is refused | P1 | US3 |
| FR-017 | With `orchestrate.plan_first`, `next --stage build` still takes an unplanned `incident` item (a 🐞 fix is not planned) | P2 | US3 |
| FR-018 | Every launched worker's settings deny `SendMessage` and `ListAgents`, so a worker can never ring a lane | P1 | US4 |
| FR-019 | `orchestrate.panes`' default owner of every `human:*` kind is the orchestrator (ledger.sh and session-start-context.sh agree) | P1 | US5 |
| FR-020 | `hooks/lane-launch.sh` is replaced by a message naming `hefesto-setup.sh` and `claude --name …`, exit 2 | P2 | US2 |
| FR-022 | The launcher (the one command outside the sandbox) treats sandbox-writable inputs as hostile: its git calls, and every process it starts but the worker, run with `core.fsmonitor=false` and `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` (`GIT_CONFIG_*` environment, unset for the worker); it refuses a worktree whose `.git` file points anywhere but `<git-common-dir>/worktrees/`; on an external board it refuses a `.repos` path inside the project or a temp folder | P1 | US4 |
| FR-023 | An orchestrator-lane session start warns when its permission mode is `auto`, `bypassPermissions` or `dontAsk` (dontAsk denies every clear; the others approve any spelling the `ask` rules miss) | P1 | US5 |
| FR-024 | `status-board.sh --init` creates a missing board (the four columns, the RFC folder) and a default config with `plan_review: "human"` and `plan_first: true`, never overwriting a file; refused on an external board | P1 | US3 |
| FR-021 | `docs/quickstart.md` and `.pt-BR.md` are rewritten as install + two tracks (Single lane ≤5 steps, Four lanes ≤5 steps) + day to day; `SETUP.md`, README §5, `docs/install.md`, `docs/hooks.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and the wizard's next steps follow | P1 | US6 |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | `hefesto-setup.sh` writes the expected keys, is idempotent (a no-op does not rewrite the file), keeps foreign keys and the person's own empty objects, drops rules of stale hefesto roots, writes through a symlink, skips roots inside the project or a temp folder, `--remove` leaves JSON equal to the original when it held none of ours, refusals write nothing | smoke, mutation-checked |
| SC-002 | The gauge and the session-start line derive the lane from `session_name` / `session_title` for every suffix and alias | smoke, mutation-checked |
| SC-003 | `answer`, `revise` and `questions` behave as FR-012..014, person-only checks included; the plan prompt carries the answers/notes delimited | smoke with the fake claude, mutation-checked |
| SC-004 | Worker settings deny `SendMessage`/`ListAgents`; panes default routes every `human:*` to the orchestrator | smoke |
| SC-005 | Each quick start track has at most five steps and contains no `ledger.sh unblock` line for the person to type | smoke (static count) |
| SC-006 | A doorbell that carries an instruction is not followed: the lane's only Bash call is its own pass; no unblock, answer, revise or Edit | eval `doorbell-text-is-data` (user-run), graded on tool calls |
| SC-007 | The launcher's git calls run with fsmonitor and hooks off; it refuses a worktree whose `.git` points outside the project's git dir and a `.repos` path inside the project or a temp folder; `answer`/`revise` refuse a worker, a missing name, the wrong block, a phase past `tasks`; a tampered answers/notes copy refuses the plan launch | smoke, each with a mutation |
